description: Engine-specific parts catalog. Placeholder assets are intentional and can be replaced without changing application logic.

parts.name: Honda B16 engine block
parts.what: The B16 block is the main aluminum-alloy structure of Honda’s 1.6-liter DOHC VTEC inline-four. It houses the four cylinders and supports the crankshaft and cylinder head.
parts.why: It keeps the cylinders aligned and carries the loads produced by combustion and the rotating assembly.
parts.where: It forms the lower central structure of the engine. The four cylinder bores are machined into the deck at the top, with the crankcase below.

parts.name: Crankshaft
parts.what: The crankshaft converts the pistons’ up-and-down movement into rotation.
parts.why: Its rotation is the mechanical output that ultimately drives the transmission.
parts.where: It sits inside the lower crankcase and is supported by the main bearing bridges.
parts.installationReason: The crankshaft is installed in the block and supported by the main bearing bridges.

parts.name: Main bearings and bearing caps
parts.what: Five main bearing locations support the crankshaft. The bearing shells provide the precision surfaces, while the caps secure the crankshaft from below.
parts.why: The main bearings support the crankshaft while allowing it to rotate with a controlled oil film.
parts.where: The bearing shells sit at the five main journal supports, with the lower caps fitted underneath the crankshaft.
parts.installationReason: Install the crankshaft first. The five main bearing cap assemblies are then fitted and secured beneath the crankshaft.

parts.name: Pistons and connecting rods
parts.what: Four pistons slide inside the cylinder liners. Connecting rods link each piston to a crankshaft throw.
parts.why: Combustion pressure pushes the pistons down, and the connecting rods transfer that force to the crankshaft.
parts.where: The pistons fit into the four cylinder bores, with their connecting rods extending down to the crankshaft.
parts.installationReason: The connecting rods need the crankshaft and main bearing caps in place so their big ends can attach to the crank throws.

parts.name: Oil pump assembly
parts.what: The oil pump draws oil from the sump and pressurizes it so oil can circulate through the engine.
parts.why: A steady supply of pressurized oil lubricates the crankshaft bearings and other moving parts.
parts.where: The pump mounts to the timing-belt end of the B-series block, around the front of the crankshaft.
parts.installationReason: Install the rotating assembly first. The oil pump mounts at the timing-belt end of the block around the crankshaft nose.

parts.name: Oil pickup tube and screen
parts.what: The pickup tube draws oil from the sump through a screened inlet.
parts.why: The screen helps keep larger debris from entering the oil pump.
parts.where: It connects to the oil pump and extends down into the oil pan.

parts.name: Oil pan / sump
parts.what: The oil pan is the reservoir that holds engine oil when it is not circulating through the engine.
parts.why: The oil pump draws oil from the sump and sends it to bearings and other moving parts.
parts.where: It bolts to the underside of the crankcase.
parts.installationReason: Install the crankshaft and connecting rod assemblies before closing the bottom of the crankcase with the oil pan.

parts.name: Oil pan gasket / sealant
parts.what: The oil pan seal closes the joint between the sump and crankcase.
parts.why: It helps prevent engine oil from leaking at the pan flange.
parts.where: It sits between the oil pan flange and the bottom of the block.

parts.name: Cylinder head gasket
parts.what: The head gasket is a thin, carefully sealed layer between the engine block and cylinder head.
parts.why: It seals combustion pressure and keeps coolant and engine oil passages separated.
parts.where: It sits on the machined deck surface at the top of the engine block.
parts.installationReason: Install the piston and rod assemblies before sealing the top of the block with the head gasket.

parts.name: Cylinder head
parts.what: The cylinder head closes the top of the cylinders and contains the combustion chambers and valve passages.
parts.why: It seals the cylinders and routes incoming air and outgoing exhaust gases.
parts.where: It bolts to the top of the engine block over the head gasket.
parts.installationReason: The cylinder head sits on the head gasket. The gasket must be in place first.

parts.name: Cylinder head bolts
parts.what: Head bolts clamp the cylinder head and gasket to the engine block.
parts.why: Correct clamping load helps maintain the combustion and fluid seals.
parts.where: They pass through the cylinder head into the block’s threaded holes.

parts.name: Valves and valve springs
parts.what: The intake and exhaust valves open and close the ports; springs return them to their seats.
parts.why: They control the flow of air-fuel mixture and exhaust through each cylinder.
parts.where: They install in the cylinder head’s valve guides and spring seats.

parts.name: Intake and exhaust camshafts
parts.what: The two overhead camshafts operate the intake and exhaust valves.
parts.why: Their lobes determine valve lift and timing.
parts.where: They sit in the cylinder head above the valves.

parts.name: Rocker arms and VTEC assembly
parts.what: The rocker assembly transfers camshaft motion to the valves and includes the VTEC switching mechanism.
parts.why: It controls valve motion and enables the engine’s variable-lift operating mode.
parts.where: It mounts along the camshaft and valve assemblies in the cylinder head.

parts.name: Camshaft caps
parts.what: Camshaft caps retain and support the camshafts in the cylinder head.
parts.why: They maintain camshaft alignment and bearing clearance.
parts.where: They bolt over the camshaft journals on the cylinder head.

parts.name: Camshaft gears
parts.what: Cam gears connect the timing belt to the camshafts.
parts.why: They keep camshaft rotation synchronized with the crankshaft.
parts.where: They mount on the ends of the intake and exhaust camshafts.

parts.name: Water pump
parts.what: The water pump circulates coolant through the engine and radiator.
parts.why: Coolant flow carries heat away from the engine.
parts.where: It mounts at the timing-belt end of the engine.

parts.name: Timing belt tensioner
parts.what: The tensioner maintains the correct tension in the timing belt.
parts.why: Correct tension helps prevent belt slip and timing errors.
parts.where: It mounts beside the timing belt path.

parts.name: Timing belt
parts.what: The timing belt synchronizes crankshaft and camshaft rotation.
parts.why: It keeps valve events synchronized with piston movement.
parts.where: It loops around the crankshaft gear, cam gears and tensioner.

parts.name: Timing belt covers
parts.what: The timing covers enclose the timing belt and pulleys.
parts.why: They help protect the timing components from debris.
parts.where: They attach around the front timing drive.
parts.installationReason: Install the timing drive components before fitting the protective covers.

parts.name: Intake manifold
parts.what: The intake manifold distributes incoming air to the four cylinders.
parts.why: It helps each cylinder receive the air needed for combustion.
parts.where: It bolts to one side of the cylinder head and routes air through four runners.
parts.installationReason: The intake manifold bolts to the cylinder head and must align with its intake ports.

parts.name: Fuel rail and injectors
parts.what: The fuel rail supplies pressurized fuel to the injectors.
parts.why: The injectors meter fuel into the intake ports.
parts.where: The rail mounts along the intake manifold and holds one injector per cylinder.

parts.name: Throttle body
parts.what: The throttle body regulates how much air enters the intake manifold.
parts.why: It responds to driver throttle input and controls engine airflow.
parts.where: It attaches to the inlet of the intake manifold.

parts.name: Exhaust manifold
parts.what: The exhaust manifold collects hot gases leaving the four cylinders.
parts.why: It routes exhaust from each cylinder into a common outlet.
parts.where: It bolts to the opposite side of the cylinder head and aligns with the exhaust ports.
parts.installationReason: The exhaust manifold bolts to the cylinder head and must align with its exhaust ports.

parts.name: Distributor and ignition components
parts.what: The distributor routes high-voltage ignition to the correct spark plug in firing order.
parts.why: It helps ignite the air-fuel mixture at the correct time.
parts.where: It mounts at the end of the cylinder head/camshaft drive.

parts.name: Alternator assembly
parts.what: The alternator converts mechanical rotation into electrical power.
parts.why: It supplies electrical power while the engine runs and recharges the vehicle battery.
parts.where: It mounts on a bracket at the front accessory drive and is driven by the belt.
parts.installationReason: The alternator is driven by the accessory belt, so the crankshaft pulley must be installed first.

parts.name: Starter motor
parts.what: The starter motor cranks the engine during startup.
parts.why: It turns the crankshaft until combustion can sustain engine operation.
parts.where: It mounts to the transmission bellhousing at the engine block.

parts.name: Accessory brackets
parts.what: Brackets support accessories and maintain their alignment.
parts.why: They hold the alternator and other driven components in the correct position.
parts.where: They bolt to the engine block at accessory mounting bosses.

parts.name: Accessory pulleys and belts
parts.what: Pulleys and belts transfer crankshaft rotation to engine accessories.
parts.why: They drive the alternator and other belt-driven components.
parts.where: They mount on the crankshaft and accessory shafts.

parts.name: Coolant hoses and thermostat housing
parts.what: The hoses route coolant between the engine and cooling system; the thermostat housing contains the thermostat connection.
parts.why: They manage coolant circulation and engine temperature.
parts.where: They connect to the cylinder head, block and radiator circuit.

parts.name: Flywheel
parts.what: The flywheel provides rotating mass and a friction surface for the clutch.
parts.why: It transfers crankshaft torque into the manual clutch assembly.
parts.where: It bolts to the rear of the crankshaft.

parts.name: Clutch disc
parts.what: The clutch disc transfers torque from the flywheel to the transmission input shaft.
parts.why: It allows the engine to be coupled to or disconnected from the transmission.
parts.where: It sits between the flywheel and pressure plate.

parts.name: Clutch pressure plate
parts.what: The pressure plate clamps the clutch disc against the flywheel.
parts.why: It transmits engine torque through friction when engaged.
parts.where: It bolts to the flywheel over the clutch disc.

parts.name: Release bearing and clutch fork
parts.what: The release bearing and fork disengage the clutch when the pedal is pressed.
parts.why: They allow smooth gear changes by releasing clutch clamp force.
parts.where: They operate at the front of the transmission bellhousing.

parts.name: Transmission bellhousing
parts.what: The bellhousing joins the transmission to the engine and encloses the clutch.
parts.why: It aligns the transmission input shaft with the crankshaft.
parts.where: It bolts to the rear of the engine block.

parts.name: 5-speed transmission casing
parts.what: The transmission case houses the gears, shafts and differential.
parts.why: It supports and protects the gearbox components.
parts.where: It bolts to the bellhousing and encloses the geartrain.

parts.name: Transmission gears and shafts
parts.what: Gear pairs and shafts provide the selected gear ratios.
parts.why: They convert engine speed and torque to suit vehicle speed and load.
parts.where: They are supported inside the transmission case.

parts.name: Synchronizers and shift forks
parts.what: Synchronizers match gear speeds while shift forks move the sliding components.
parts.why: They help engage gears smoothly without gear clash.
parts.where: They install on the transmission shafts inside the case.

parts.name: Differential assembly
parts.what: The differential splits torque between the drive axles while allowing different wheel speeds.
parts.why: It allows the driven wheels to rotate at different speeds in a turn.
parts.where: It is housed in the transaxle case.

parts.name: Transmission side cover
parts.what: The side cover closes the transmission case opening.
parts.why: It retains and protects internal transmission components.
parts.where: It bolts to the side of the transmission case.

parts.name: Axles and CV joints
parts.what: The axles transfer torque from the differential to the driven wheels.
parts.why: CV joints transmit torque while accommodating suspension movement and steering angle.
parts.where: They connect to the differential outputs and wheel hubs.

parts.name: Engine mounts
parts.what: Engine mounts secure the engine to the vehicle chassis.
parts.why: They support engine weight and isolate vibration.
parts.where: They attach to mounting bosses on the engine and chassis.

parts.name: Transmission mounts
parts.what: Transmission mounts support the gearbox and connect it to the chassis.
parts.why: They control drivetrain movement and vibration.
parts.where: They attach to the transmission case and chassis.

parts.name: Sensors and wiring harness
parts.what: Sensors monitor engine conditions and the harness connects electrical components to the ECU.
parts.why: They provide the signals and power needed for engine management.
parts.where: The harness routes around the engine and connects to sensors, injectors and ignition components.

parts.name: Spark plugs
parts.what: Spark plugs ignite the compressed air-fuel mixture in each cylinder.
parts.why: They initiate combustion.
parts.where: They thread into the cylinder head, one per cylinder.

parts.name: Engine fluids
parts.what: Engine oil and coolant fill their respective circuits.
parts.why: The fluids lubricate moving parts and carry away heat.
parts.where: Oil fills the sump; coolant fills the engine cooling passages and connected circuit.

parts.name: Final inspection
parts.what: A final inspection checks assembly completeness, fasteners, clearances and fluid readiness.
parts.why: It helps catch assembly issues before operation.
parts.where: It is the final verification stage after all required components are installed.

parts.name: Oil filter assembly
parts.what: The oil filter removes contaminants from the engine oil.
parts.why: Filtering debris helps protect bearings and other precision moving surfaces.
parts.where: It mounts to an angled boss on the side of the engine block.
parts.installationReason: The oil filter mounts to the side of the engine block.

parts.name: Crankshaft accessory pulley
parts.what: The grooved crankshaft pulley is driven directly by the crankshaft.
parts.why: It transfers crankshaft rotation to the accessory belt.
parts.where: It mounts at the front end of the crankshaft.
parts.installationReason: The crankshaft pulley mounts on the crankshaft nose outside the front cover.

parts.name: Accessory drive belt
parts.what: The accessory belt transfers rotation from the crankshaft pulley to the alternator pulley.
parts.why: It allows the crankshaft to drive engine accessories.
parts.where: It loops around the crankshaft pulley and alternator pulley.
parts.installationReason: The accessory belt must route around the installed crankshaft and alternator pulleys.

parts.name: Valvetrain and dual overhead camshafts
parts.what: The two overhead camshafts operate the intake and exhaust valves.
parts.why: Their lobes determine valve lift and timing.
parts.where: They sit in the cylinder head above the valves.
parts.installationReason: The valves, springs, and camshafts are installed in the cylinder head.

parts.name: Valve cover
parts.what: Head bolts clamp the cylinder head and gasket to the engine block.
parts.why: Correct clamping load helps maintain the combustion and fluid seals.
parts.where: They pass through the cylinder head into the block’s threaded holes.
parts.installationReason: The valve cover encloses the camshafts and must be installed after the valvetrain.
